issues.legal_issue: Estoppel may be raised as a defence to a statutory right of pre-emption despite the vendor’s failure to give the required notice when the right is private and the failure does not make the transfer void.
material_facts: The vendor did not give the notice required by the pre-emption legislation.
The pre-emptor knew of the sale and asserted a right to pre-empt it.
The legislation did not provide that failure to give notice made the sale void.
issues.conclusion: Estoppel could be raised as a defence. The notice requirement was a condition of the transfer’s validity, not a rule whose breach rendered the sale void; the pre-emption right was private and could be waived expressly or by conduct.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 115 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, estoppel is an equitable defence that may prevent a person from asserting a claim inconsistent with conduct that induced another to act. There can be no estoppel against a statute where it would enforce what is illegal or void, or defeat a public interest. But a waivable condition of validity is distinct from a rule whose breach makes a transaction void. The court relied on sections 8 and 9 of the Rajasthan Pre-emption Act, 1966, and on Shalimar Tar Products Ltd. v. H.C. Sharma, Equitable Life Assurance Society of the United States v. Reed, Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh, Radha Kishan v. Shridhar, and Pateshwari Partab Narain Singh v. Sitaram. It overruled Jethmal v. Sajanumal.

rule.if: preemption_case and notice_omitted and notice_failure_does_not_void_transfer and preemption_right_is_private

predicates.preemption_case: The proceeding seeks to enforce a right to take a transfer in place of its purchaser.
predicates.notice_omitted: The person making the transfer did not give the notice required to alert a potential pre-emptor.
predicates.notice_failure_does_not_void_transfer: The governing law does not make the transfer void merely because the required notice was not given.
predicates.preemption_right_is_private: The right being asserted belongs to the claimant alone and does not protect a public or community interest.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption proceeding concerns a private right and omission of notice does not void the transfer, estoppel may be raised as a defence.

issues.legal_issue: A pre-emptor is estopped from asserting the right after knowingly assisting construction on the purchased property without objection and claiming pre-emption only after construction is complete.
material_facts: The pre-emptor knew of the sale soon after it occurred.
The pre-emptor assisted the purchaser in raising construction and did not object while construction proceeded.
After construction was completed, the pre-emptor gave notice claiming the right and later filed a pre-emption suit.
issues.conclusion: The pre-emptor’s conduct was inequitable, and the claim was barred by estoppel. The appeal was allowed and the first appellate court’s dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Estoppel is an equitable rule that prevents a person from taking advantage of conduct that induced another to act in good faith. Applying section 115 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, and the principles in Bishan Singh v. Khazan Singh and Radha Kishan v. Shridhar, the court held that a pre-emption claim could not be used to defeat the purchaser’s position after the claimant’s conduct had indicated acquiescence.

rule.if: preemption_case and preemptor_knew_of_sale and preemptor_assisted_construction and preemptor_did_not_object_during_construction and preemptor_claimed_after_construction

predicates.preemption_case: The proceeding seeks to enforce a right to take a transfer in place of its purchaser.
predicates.preemptor_knew_of_sale: The claimant knew that the property had been sold.
predicates.preemptor_assisted_construction: The claimant helped the purchaser carry out construction on the property.
predicates.preemptor_did_not_object_during_construc: The claimant did not object to the purchaser’s ownership while construction was underway.
predicates.preemptor_claimed_after_construction: The claimant asserted the right to pre-empt only after construction was complete.

issues.definition: In a pre-emption proceeding, a claimant who knew of the sale, assisted construction without objecting, and claimed the right only after construction was complete is barred from asserting the claim.
